The Care Support Readiness Checklist

Who will be there, what to write down and what to ask before your husband's care changes.

Download PDF

Your husband's care is about to change, and the plan so far is that everyone will pitch in. This list turns that into things you can map, write down and ask in the days you have. Check what you've done. An unchecked box is something still to do. It says nothing about the plan, or about you.

Map

Write down

Ask

What this checklist doesn't do

It helps you map, write down and ask. It doesn't tell you whether the arrangement is safe or whether the help is enough, and a page with every box checked isn't a safety clearance. That judgment belongs to the people who assess your husband.

Ready for the next step?

You've mapped who will be there and written down what is still open. The care interview goes through your husband's situation area by area, so the hours on your map sit beside what he needs during them, and turns your answers into a Family Care Profile you can bring to any care conversation.

Where this comes from

Items marked 1 follow Medicare's discharge planning checklist. The item marked 2 names places the CDC's home checklist asks families to look at. The rest come from the Family Care Roadmap's own working list for this step.

  1. Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services, Your Discharge Planning Checklist (CMS Product No. 11376)
  2. Centers for Disease Control and Prevention, Check for Safety: A Home Fall Prevention Checklist for Older Adults (STEADI brochure, 2018)
